case.case_title: Rassool and others v. Cader, Director for Mosques and Muslim Charitable Trusts and others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1993] 2 Sri LR.

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the suspension of the petitioners from office as Special Trustees of a Mosque violated their fundamental right to equality before the law and equal protection under Article 12(1).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed that their suspension was discriminatory and violated their right to equality and equal protection under the law.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the suspension was lawful under the Wakfs Act and justified by the petitioners' political activities within the Mosque premises.
key_facts: Petitioners were Special Trustees of a Mosque appointed by the Wakfs Board.
The 1st petitioner was a political candidate and engaged in political activities.
The 1st respondent suspended the petitioners ex parte without inquiry.
No evidence was produced that the petitioners misused Mosque premises for political purposes.
The suspension was challenged as ultra vires and discriminatory.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 12(1) guarantees equality before the law and equal protection, which prohibits arbitrary or discriminatory treatment by public authorities. Suspension without inquiry was ultra vires and violated the principle of equality.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the suspension was made without proper inquiry and was not supported by evidence of misuse of Mosque premises. The 1st respondent acted beyond statutory powers, thus denying the petitioners equal protection under the law.
principles_established: Public officials must act within statutory powers and provide fair inquiry before suspension.
Equality before the law requires non-arbitrary and non-discriminatory treatment.
Ex parte suspension without inquiry is without jurisdiction and violates fundamental rights.
precedents_cited: Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu AIR 1974 SC 555

outcome.holding: The court held that the suspension violated Article 12(1) as it was ultra vires and denied the petitioners equal protection under the law.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declaration of violation of Article 12(1) and related reliefs.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court's reasoning as the petitioners challenged the suspension as a denial of equality and equal protection under the law.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found the suspension was without jurisdiction and in excess of statutory powers, thus violating the petitioners' right to equal protection under Article 12(1).
